messages.subject: Constrained mixture model
parts:
Hi,

Thanks for the software and for the support provided in this list.

I’m trying to estimate a mixture of two constrained multivariate normal models. In one model, the first mean is constrained between 0 and 0.95, and the other means are constrained between 0 and 1, and in the second, the fist mean is constrained between 0.95 and 1 and the rest of the means are constrained between 0 and 1.

I'm attaching my R code (stan function followed by simulated data). The estimation process does not end with the correct mixture of the data I simulate. Estimates also do not converge on all the parameters.

Many thanks,
Mattan

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Constrained mixture model
parts:
I didn't see the simulation code, but obviously that's going to
need to match for this to work. Otherwise, your model looks OK,
though I don't understand what it's for or why you coded it this way.

What's not converging here? And I take it running more iterations
didn't help? Will it stay in the right area if you initialize with
the simulated values?

Some detailed comments.

1. Does it looks like one chain converges? You get identifiability
problems with label switching because which component is one and which
is zero is not identified.

2. The coding of mu in terms of mu0 is awkward in that you're
ignore mu0[1,1] and mu0[2,1]. Though that's not a dealbreaker because
they're constrained to be between 0 and 1 and hence proper, it will
slow things down and lead to output that makes no sense.

Better would be to define mu0 as [2,K-1] and then use a loop to
define mu.

3. Everything will work better with a Cholesky-based parameterization
of the correlation matrix Omega. See the most recent manual's chapter
on regression --- there's a section on multivariate priors. This shouldn't
change the fit, but should help with numerical stability and efficiency.

4. I find the names "one" and "notOne" confusing for names of parameters.
And just to check --- you only want this constraint on the first column
of mu, not the remaining columns? Was the hope that this would identify
the model? A weaker constraint would be to have them ordered.

5. And why would means be contrained to (0,1) or a subinterval of it? If
you really have that constraint, maybe you want to do a GLM on the logit
of the data?


Then some speed issues.

A. It'd be faster using

real<lower=0,upper=1> theta;

and then used log(theta) and log1m(theta) for the mixture proportions rather
than using a simplex. Then you can use the two-argument log_sum_exp(a,b), which
is also faster.

But it won't generalize with this approach. How you have it is right for generalizing
to more than 2 mixture components if that's your intention.

B. It'll be faster if you declare y as

vector[K] y[N];

see the manual section on arrays vs. matrices. Not a big deal
as it won't make a big difference.
